feature: Measurement cadence runbook for repeatable ACAM comparison over time
problem: The eval pipeline (eval-fast, eval-ci-pr, eval-ci-nightly, acam-score.py, behavioral_baseline.json, eval_baseline.json) is fully implemented but there is no documented cadence for when to run each tier, how to capture a dated snapshot, how to interpret known failures in behavioral_baseline.json, or how to compare measurements over time. Without this, maintainers cannot close the diagnosis→measurement loop the ACAM research identified as the key gap to reaching Advanced.
proposed_solution: Add a 'Measurement Cadence Runbook' section to docs/EVAL_GUIDE.md covering: (1) cadence table (daily/PR: eval-fast, on merge: eval-ci-pr, weekly: eval-ci-nightly + ACAM snapshot); (2) step-by-step snapshot capture procedure producing a dated scorecard; (3) how to read behavioral_baseline.json — what expected_bool:false entries mean and how to distinguish known failures from regressions; (4) trend comparison procedure using dated snapshots; (5) documented one-liner for a full measurement pass.
acceptance_criteria: docs/EVAL_GUIDE.md contains a level-2 heading matching '^## .*Measurement Cadence' (case-insensitive): verified by `grep -qiE '^## .*measurement cadence' docs/EVAL_GUIDE.md` exit 0

Within the Measurement Cadence section (text from that heading until the next '^## ' heading), all three Makefile targets eval-fast, eval-ci-pr, and eval-ci-nightly appear, and cadence prose maps eval-fast to daily or every PR, eval-ci-pr to merge or PR merge, and eval-ci-nightly to weekly or nightly: verified by awk section extract piped to grep for each target and cadence keyword (daily|every PR, merge|PR merge, weekly|nightly) all exit 0

docs/EVAL_GUIDE.md contains a Snapshot subsection (heading containing 'Snapshot') inside the runbook with at least three numbered steps (lines matching '^[0-9]+\.') that mention acam-score and a dated output (word 'dated' or YYYY-MM-DD or timestamp): verified by awk extract of runbook section containing Snapshot heading, grep numbered steps count >= 3, grep acam-score and dated pattern

docs/EVAL_GUIDE.md documents behavioral_baseline.json interpretation: runbook text references tests/eval/fixtures/behavioral_baseline.json (or behavioral_baseline.json) AND expected_bool AND explains that false marks a known/accepted failure not a regression (grep matches behavioral_baseline and expected_bool; section also matches known failure prose via known.*fail|false.*known|not a regression)

docs/EVAL_GUIDE.md contains a Trend or trend comparison subsection (heading containing 'Trend') that explains comparing two dated snapshots using diff or compare against snapshot or baseline: verified by awk extract from Trend heading until next ## and grep -qiE '(diff|compare)' plus grep -qiE '(snapshot|baseline)' on same extract

docs/EVAL_GUIDE.md contains a Full Measurement Pass subsection (heading containing 'Full Measurement Pass') with a fenced code block or inline command showing make eval-fast as the one-liner full static measurement pass (make eval-fast already invokes acam-score.py per Makefile): verified by grep -qi 'full measurement pass' and grep -q 'make eval-fast' docs/EVAL_GUIDE.md

Runbook documents eval_baseline.json unseeded behavior: text mentions aggregate_score null or unseeded for a tier and states regression check exits 0 with a warning (not a hard fail): verified by grep -qiE 'eval_baseline|aggregate_score' docs/EVAL_GUIDE.md and grep -qiE 'null|unseeded' and grep -qiE 'warning|exit 0' on runbook section or doc

Runbook documents static-only snapshot when CURSOR_API_KEY is unavailable: prose states eval-fast plus acam-score.py produces a valid comparable ACAM scorecard without session tier: verified by grep -qiE 'CURSOR_API_KEY|API key' and grep -qi 'acam-score' and grep -qiE 'eval-fast|static' docs/EVAL_GUIDE.md within runbook section

Trend comparison subsection warns that snapshots older than ~30 days or across major rule/model changes may be noisy and recommends comparing same model version: verified by grep -qiE '30 day|model version|rule change' docs/EVAL_GUIDE.md
edge_cases: behavioral_baseline.json entries with expected_bool:false — runbook must explain these represent known behavioral gaps (current model limitations) accepted at baseline-seed time, not regressions (covered by AC4)
eval_baseline.json aggregate_score:null for nightly tier — runbook must note that null means unseeded (no CI data yet) and regression check exits 0 with a warning rather than failing (covered by AC7)

Snapshot capture when CURSOR_API_KEY is unavailable — runbook must note that a static-only snapshot (eval-fast + acam-score.py) is valid and still produces a comparable ACAM scorecard without the session tier (covered by AC8)

Stale snapshots (dated >30 days) — trend comparison section should note that comparing across major rule changes may produce noise; recommend comparing snapshots from the same model version (covered by AC9)
verification_method:
Run from repo root (all must exit 0):
DOC=docs/EVAL_GUIDE.md
RUNBOOK=$(awk '/^## .*[Mm]easurement [Cc]adence/{p=1; next} p && /^## /{exit} p' "$DOC")
# AC1
grep -qiE '^## .*measurement cadence' "$DOC"
# AC2
echo "$RUNBOOK" | grep -q eval-fast && echo "$RUNBOOK" | grep -q eval-ci-pr && echo "$RUNBOOK" | grep -q eval-ci-nightly
echo "$RUNBOOK" | grep -qiE 'daily|every PR'
echo "$RUNBOOK" | grep -qiE 'merge|PR merge'
echo "$RUNBOOK" | grep -qiE 'weekly|nightly'
# AC3
SNAP=$(echo "$RUNBOOK" | awk '/^### .*[Ss]napshot|^## .*[Ss]napshot/{p=1; next} p && /^###? / && !/[Ss]napshot/{exit} p')
echo "$SNAP" | grep -qi acam-score
echo "$SNAP" | grep -qiE 'dated|YYYY-MM-DD|timestamp'
test $(echo "$SNAP" | grep -cE '^[0-9]+\.') -ge 3
# AC4
grep -qi behavioral_baseline "$DOC" && grep -qi expected_bool "$DOC"
grep -qiE 'known.*fail|false.*known|not a regression|known failure' "$DOC"
# AC5
TREND=$(echo "$RUNBOOK" | awk '/^### .*[Tt]rend|^## .*[Tt]rend/{p=1; next} p && /^## /{exit} p')
echo "$TREND" | grep -qiE 'diff|compare'
echo "$TREND" | grep -qiE 'snapshot|baseline'
# AC6
grep -qi 'full measurement pass' "$DOC" && grep -q 'make eval-fast' "$DOC"
# AC7
grep -qiE 'eval_baseline|aggregate_score' "$DOC" && grep -qiE 'null|unseeded' "$DOC" && grep -qiE 'warning|exit 0' "$DOC"
# AC8
echo "$RUNBOOK" | grep -qiE 'CURSOR_API_KEY|API key'
echo "$RUNBOOK" | grep -qi acam-score
echo "$RUNBOOK" | grep -qiE 'eval-fast|static'
# AC9
grep -qiE '30 day|model version|rule change' "$DOC"
